rationale: Verified against package source and hash-bound reference files. (1) Input claims: the staged LuxC.sto is the wheel fixture (sha256 e2cf20e9…): 13 sequences (#=GF SQ 13), carry-lines ID/AC/DE, and legacy two-pair GA/TC/NC lines; Easel's Stockholm parser (esl_msafile_stockholm.c:553-595) stores exactly the first two reals of each cutoff line, p7_builder.annotate copies them verbatim, and the plan7 writer emits 'GA %.1f %.1f' — so the reference GA/TC/NC values (-133.50 -133.50 / -133.50 -133.50 / -133.70 -133.70) are exactly what any HMMER3-conforming build produces, and the acceptance rules compare these reference values, so 'carried through unchanged' has a fixed, format-defined meaning. (2) Reference domtbl verified: 12 rows, all single-domain, strictly distinct full-sequence E-values in the documented hmmsearch order, query name/accession/length consistent with the HMM — the addendum's no-ties claim is true. (3) Grader: domtbl column indices correct for the 22-field layout; HMM tokenization excludes only banner/DATE/COM; tolerances (2e-5 for 5-decimal prints, 0.06/0.006 for 1-/2-decimal prints, 5% relative E-value with max-magnitude denominator) are disclosed publicly and match the constants; integer tolerance 0.5 is effectively exact for integer-valued fields; no hardcoded answers or check-name detection; reference read at runtime. (4) All 18 controls executed on one candidate hash with the reported outcomes: reference/recomputed/alternative pass; empty/missing/misplaced (extra outputs/ nesting) fail correctly; all 10 wrong-solution probes fail exactly the intended scientific checks including boundary-tolerance and non-finite rejection, and the valid-representation probe stays inside the granted freedoms and passes. (5) Repair audit: only the w-domtbl-coordinates-and-description expected-check annotation changed (['domtbl_hits','domtbl_structure'] -> ['domtbl_hits']); I independently verified that an in-range finite integer-coordinate plus exact-text description mutation cannot fail a check whose published requirement is structural only, while domtbl_hits rejects it by value comparison — the executed control matches; no mutation script, name, kind, check, or rule was altered, so no coverage was weakened. (6) Dependency hygiene: the sole answer fixture (pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm, model body identical to the endpoint modulo banner/DATE/COM) was declared with content identity and removed with a verified receipt while execution still completes; retained LuxC fixtures are inputs, an SSI index, a reweighted variant and an hmmalign output containing no E-values/scores/HMM parameters — none is a serialization of either endpoint. (7) Source coverage: the notebook's two terminal scientific products are fully exported; the consensus inspection and print(ali) display are source-backed display exclusions whose content is retained in the two artifacts. No base-question defect found; remaining limitations (cross-engine tolerance calibration not exercised; solver-runtime persistence of the exclusion) are disclosed in the candidate's own concerns and do not affect the public contract.

source_coverage.rationale: The source (pyhmmer msa_to_hmm notebook, input paths repointed only) has exactly two terminal scientific products — the Plan7 profile HMM (builder.build_msa serialized by hmm.write) and the hmmsearch-style domain table (pipeline.search_hmm serialized by hits.write(format='domains')) — both recorded in the reference exports with verified hashes and both assigned dedicated grader checks. Every source operation in the inventory is covered: input loads (MSAFile/read, SequenceFile), build (Builder/Background/build_msa), search (Pipeline/search_hmm) and both serializations. The two display branches (hmm.consensus property inspection, print(ali)) are correctly excluded as presentation with retained counterparts — the consensus is embedded in the HMM's CONS/MAP lines and the top-hit alignment displayed is fully described by the domtbl's target identities and alignment/envelope coordinates; neither is an independent result-producing operation. No supplied intermediate replaces either endpoint: the solver receives only the byte-identical original inputs (LuxC.sto, LuxC.faa, hashes verified at staging) and must compute both the model and the search results. The precomputed answer copy in the installed distribution was removed with verified identity, receipt (excluded_files_absent true) and fresh post-exclusion execution evidence, and the retained LuxC-stem fixtures are inputs or intermediate-format files that do not serialize either endpoint — LuxC.hmmalign.sto carries no E-values, scores, threshold decisions or model parameters, and no domtbl-format LuxC fixture exists.
remaining_validation: Solver-runtime persistence of the wheel-fixture exclusion (pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm) must be re-confirmed by the controller at packaging time, as outcome.json itself records.

Cross-engine (non-pyhmmer) equivalence of the 5% relative E-value tolerance was not exercised; the candidate discloses this calibration limitation, which bounds the portability claim but does not affect the published contract.
